cards.title: Funding a first production run with crowdfunding instead of savings
cards.summary: Use a Kickstarter or Indiegogo campaign to raise the cash for your first inventory order before you ever list on Amazon.
cards.use_when: You have a product idea for your Amazon store but little capital and need to fund the first production run while simultaneously testing demand.
steps: Design the product and build marketing/buzz before paying for any inventory; the campaign itself is the spend, since backers pay first and you produce after.
Launch the crowdfunding campaign and collect the pledged money; the source raised $15,000 this way, which covered most of an initial production run.
Use the raised funds to produce the inventory, then ship the product to the backers who funded it.
Treat the campaign as a market test: pledges are evidence people want the product, which is especially useful when the item is too unique to estimate sales from existing Amazon listings.
After fulfillment, transition to Amazon with an existing buyer base and reviews to seed the launch.

If crowdfunding is not viable, the source also describes asking a friend or investor for startup cash (he gave one seller a few thousand dollars, was repaid, and shared in the upside) or, as a last resort he does not usually recommend, taking a loan.
caveats: Backers are giving you money for a promised future product; failing to deliver damages your reputation and may breach platform terms.
The $15,000 and $5,000 figures are the source's own and his students' campaign results, not typical or guaranteed outcomes.
The source says getting a loan is not recommended in most situations.

cards.title: Don't let analysis paralysis delay launch
cards.summary: Weigh the profit from launching a month sooner against the cost of the mistake you're trying to avoid, and start.
cards.use_when: You're stuck comparing manufacturers, designs or keywords and keep pushing back the date you place your first inventory order.
steps: Estimate your product's likely monthly profit; the source's example product made about $10,000/month profit, meaning each month of delay cost roughly $10,000.

Compare the delay cost to the mistake you're avoiding. Example from the source: spending a month choosing between two manufacturers to avoid a $5,000 error loses $10,000 in profit, so the 'wrong' fast choice still nets $5,000 ahead.
Accept that early mistakes are survivable if the product is good; the source lost about $5-6k of leaky jars on one run yet still made roughly $67,000 profit on the sellable first thousand units.
Pick one income method and commit to it for 3-6 months rather than dabbling across several models.
Start, then solve problems as they appear instead of trying to know everything in advance.
caveats: The $10,000/month figure is the source's own product, not a benchmark for your niche.
Speed does not excuse skipping basic product-quality checks that cause refunds and account problems.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Screening criteria for a viable Amazon product
cards.summary: Filter candidate products for price band, shippability, defensibility and personal knowledge before committing.
cards.use_when: You're choosing which product to private-label or source for your Amazon store.
steps: Set a price floor of about $15 (source's minimum); below that, Amazon fees and shipping make profitability very hard.
Ideally price under $20, because FBA fees and shipping rise sharply above that.
Reject fragile or leak-prone items: the source threw away 1,000 leaking glass jars from a 2,000-unit run; avoid glass, weak seals or anything that breaks in transit.
Avoid products Chinese manufacturers can copy exactly and undercut; the source names oversaturation, China and Amazon Basics as reasons old-style Alibaba private labeling is largely dead.
Aim to sell the best/premium version in the category so you can charge the most and earn more per unit.
Prioritize a product you're genuinely passionate about, because you'll understand and market it better through the down phases.
Validate demand before ordering: run social media or a crowdfunding campaign; the source used Kickstarter because his unique product couldn't be sized with sales-estimator tools.
caveats: The $15 minimum and under-$20 target are the source's heuristics, not universal rules; some categories support different bands.
The source acknowledges some private-label opportunity remains if you add a strong brand or other differentiator.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Using Helium 10 to find an underserved product
cards.summary: Treat Amazon as a search engine and mine search demand for phrases no one has built a product for.
cards.use_when: You need a product idea for your Amazon store and want demand data rather than guesswork.
steps: Enter a broad interest term (the source used 'cocktails') into Helium 10 and review the related product and keyword ideas it returns.
Look for specific phrases with real monthly search volume; the example found 'cocktail recipe cards' and 'bartender flashcards' had thousands of searches per month.
Check whether a product already exists for that exact phrase; the source found cocktail recipe books but no cocktflashcard product, which became the opportunity.
Build the product to match the phrase people actually type, so your listing can rank for that term.
Sign up for the free tier or use a discount link if available; verify the current Helium 10 interface and pricing before relying on any specific feature.
Combine this with a product you're passionate about so marketing is easier.
caveats: Search volume alone is not proof of profitability; check competition, price band and shippability too.
The AJ case (over $500,000 in first-year sales) is a single example, not a typical result.
Tool features and free-tier limits change; confirm current terms.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Title, main image and review count drive listing clicks
cards.summary: Optimize the three elements the source calls decisive for click-through and conversion on an Amazon listing.
cards.use_when: You're writing or revising a product title and main image, or diagnosing why a live listing gets no sales.
steps: Put the main target keyword at the very front of the title; Amazon weighs early words more and shoppers instantly confirm relevance. Don't lead with your brand unless you're an established brand like Nike, which still leads with the product.
Write the title so a shopper immediately recognizes the match; the source's principle is 'don't make users think.'
Use a clean, clear main image that fills the frame with minimal white space, since the image sits on a white background and must pop.
Show the product itself, not your box or logo; a small logo is fine but the product must dominate.
Treat review count as a purchase prerequisite; the source argues a listing with only three to five reviews won't sell and you should not believe in a product you can't get reviewed.
Seed early reviews through a launch group built before launch (Facebook group, Instagram or email list), which produced 75 reviews in his first week and pushed ranking toward page one.
caveats: The source states his review-solicitation methods are against Amazon's terms of service and says to proceed at your own risk; Amazon can remove reviews and crack down.
Amazon has title-format rules that the source says the platform often doesn't enforce strictly, but that is his experience, not a guarantee.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Writing bullet points and secondary images that convert
cards.summary: Lead with benefits and show ownership scenarios to make an online shopper mentally experience the product.
cards.use_when: You're building the bullet points and image stack on your Amazon product page.
steps: Write bullets for the customer, not the algorithm, though you can weave keywords in naturally.
Translate features into benefits: instead of '19g of fat,' say the product gives sustained, long-lasting energy.
Include a 100% money-back guarantee bullet even though every Amazon product effectively carries one; it reassures buyers, and the source says he was taken up on it only once in a year.
Use the secondary images to show what owning the product is like: real people using it, it in real settings, and answers to common questions (for his food product, ways to eat it and recipes).
Put modest effort into the text description; the source estimates 99% of buyers decide from the main image, reviews, title, bullets and other images.
Audit your own buying behavior on Amazon to see which of these elements actually drove your last purchase.
caveats: Bullet and image content cannot fix a bad product or a duplicate, undifferentiated offer.
The guarantee-bullet tactic is a persuasion device, not a new policy; returns still cost you.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Choosing an FBA manufacturer and avoiding manufacturing losses
cards.summary: Screen manufacturers for simple per-unit pricing, short lead times and clear contracts before you commit.
cards.use_when: You're selecting a supplier to produce your Amazon inventory and want to avoid costly production-run surprises.
steps: Insist on simple per-unit pricing; the source rejected a manufacturer that billed per production day after quoting an estimate, which then stretched to five days.
Check how fast they can produce and reorder, because long lead times cause stockouts; the source lost about $5,000 in sales waiting on a slow manufacturer.
Get the contract terms, including any buried fees, reviewed before signing; the source was effectively out $10,000 from fees buried in a long contract that even his lawyer missed.
Sit with a printed spec for every component: no tear notch on pouches cost $2,000 to fix by hand, and leaky pouches forced him to discard and clean units.
Keep every document — bill of lading, receipts, contracts — safe; he lost a pallet claim because the bill of lading couldn't be located.
Consider US manufacturers found through sourcing directories if you want to reduce copying risk.
caveats: The source notes outright manufacturer scams are not that common, and the one that hit him was US-based.
A lawyer review did not catch the buried fees in his case, so review contract economics yourself as well.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Switching from FBM to FBA to multiply sales
cards.summary: Compare self-fulfillment against FBA on Prime eligibility, postage cost and sales volume before choosing.
cards.use_when: You're deciding how to ship orders for your Amazon store: from your own warehouse (FBM) or through Amazon FBA.
steps: Recognize that FBA makes products Prime-eligible with 2-day shipping, and most Amazon shoppers are Prime members who prefer Prime-eligible listings.
Test the switch on part of your catalog; the source's sales for converted products rose 4-5x after moving from FBM to FBA.
Recheck the cost assumption: he found FBA fees were actually lower than what he was paying in postage, so he saved money as well as growing sales.
Account for the storage-fee risk you were avoiding by holding inventory yourself, and manage it with the inventory-turn practices in this deck.
Keep some fulfillment flexibility only if a product genuinely can't ship through FBA.
caveats: The 4-5x increase is the source's own product experience, not a guaranteed outcome.
FBA introduces storage and long-term storage fees that self-fulfillment does not.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Ordering the right amount of inventory to avoid fees and stockouts
cards.summary: Balance Amazon storage costs against lost sales by ordering roughly six months of inventory and cycling aged units.
cards.use_when: You're planning a replenishment order or see units sitting long in Amazon's warehouse.
steps: Order roughly six months of inventory so that if the product sells faster than expected you still have time to reorder from your manufacturer.
Watch stock levels closely; a one-week stockout on his first product cost at least $3,000 in lost sales.
Monitor aged inventory in Seller Central, and if units approach the one-year mark, request Amazon return them to you and ship them back so the clock resets.
Do that return-and-resend whenever the round-trip shipping is cheaper than the long-term storage fee, which the source says is usually the case.
Avoid over-ordering perishable or expiring goods; he discarded a few hundred units of an expiring product but still made about $10,000 profit on that run.
caveats: The ~$0.75 per cubic foot per month storage and ~$6 per cubic foot long-term figures are from the source and from the period he describes; verify current Amazon fee schedules.
Amazon penalizes chronic stockouts with lower search placement, and the source says it can even blacklist you.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Auditing Amazon fee overcharges
cards.summary: Monitor your seller account for incorrect fees and reimburse claims before the window closes.
cards.use_when: You're running a live Amazon store and want to recover money lost to overbilling or missing inventory.
steps: Review FBA fees, storage fees and other charges regularly rather than assuming they're correct; the source says he lost over $3,000 to overcharges.
When you find an error, open a case by email with Amazon promptly; the source says they usually fix it if you catch it early.
If you wait too long, expect Amazon to refuse reimbursement for the overcharge.
Consider third-party reimbursement software that scans your account for overcharges and money Amazon owes you; the source wishes he'd used one earlier.
Treat any Amazon-carried shipment as evidence you must document: keep the bill of lading and every receipt so you can dispute a claim that a pallet never arrived.
caveats: Reimbursement tool names, features and fees change; verify the current tool and interface before buying.
The source lost a missing-pallet claim because the bill of lading wasn't kept, so retain all shipping paperwork.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Differentiating against oversaturation and copycats
cards.summary: Sell a differentiated 'passion product' and expect competitors to grow the category rather than steal your share.
cards.use_when: You're evaluating whether a niche is too crowded or deciding how unique your product needs to be.
steps: Diagnose the problem as specific saturated categories, not Amazon as a whole; the source notes Amazon has over 9 million sellers but only about 1 million active, and cites that 43%+ of sellers have made at least $100,000.
When everyone is selling the same category, zag: look for a product no one else offers rather than another Alibaba item with your sticker on it.
Build a 'passion product' that is genuinely better than the competition, supported by strong branding.

Expect first-mover advantage to hold: the source's first keto nut butter saw competitors enter in year two and sales rose from about $300,000 to about $400,000 as the category's customer pool expanded.
Plan your defensibility early: a provisional patent (about $75 for up to a year of protection), an NN agreement (non-disclosure, non-use, non-circumvention) with your manufacturer, or a China patent.
Compete on branding and social media, which the source argues is where he can beat overseas copiers.
caveats: The source rates China-related copying risk as 10 out of 10 for concern before mitigation, and notes NDAs don't work in China the way an NN agreement can.
Sales-growth-through-competition is his own product's example, not a rule that applies to every niche.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Rating recession and inflation risk for an Amazon launch
cards.summary: Assess macro fears by category and adjust pricing and product choice instead of delaying.
cards.use_when: You're deciding whether to launch or which category to enter given recession or inflation concerns.
steps: Note that the source cites 50% of Fortune 500 companies being started during recessions, and that Amazon sales have risen every year regardless of the stock market.
Rate outright recession fear around 5 out of 10; certain categories drop, but groceries, baby items, pet items and small indulgences like candy tend to hold up.
Choose a category whose demand is recession-resistant if you expect a downturn, or position your product as an affordable pleasure.
Handle inflation by raising your prices as your input and shipping costs rise; as an owner you can adjust, unlike a salaried worker.
Don't let macro predictions become analysis paralysis; the source warns that worst-case focus keeps people from ever starting.
caveats: Specific statistics (50% of Fortune 500, 23% shipping-cost increase, 43% of sellers earning $100k+) are the source's claims; verify before using them in your own planning.
The source himself says no one actually knows where the economy is going.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx
